summary: We are testing whether a budget-saving 'lean Phase 1' (batch=128, 4 evals per tier) can correctly identify the optimal hardware tier for subsequent Phase 2 optimization, and whether TPE-based Phase 2 can recover the remaining performance gap. This is iteration 4, building on prior probe data showing that batch-size sensitivity during tier ranking is the critical variable determining whether the two-phase search strategy succeeds or fails.
key_points: h-main (H100, rate=5000): Predicts lean Phase 1 correctly picks TP=4/2 as optimal tier, and TPE Phase 2 (46 evals) reaches within 1% of the full-budget score (0.176474) in ≤20 evals across 3 seeds — because relative tier rankings are preserved even when all tiers are batch-bottlenecked at 128.

h-control-negative (H100, rate=500): Predicts lean Phase 1 picks the WRONG tier (TP=2/4 instead of TP=8/1) with a ≥20% unrecoverable deficit — because at low rate, TP=8/1 is uniquely throttled by batch=128 while TP=2/4 is unaffected, inverting the true ranking. Phase 2 within the wrong tier cannot fix this.

h-ablation (H100, rate=5000): Predicts TPE Phase 2 converges faster than Latin Hypercube Sampling to 95% of within-tier optimal (0.1676) in ≥2/3 seeds — because TPE exploits the strong monotone batch→score signal (5 ordered values spanning 0.077–0.176) that LHS ignores.

h-robustness (6 conditions: rate={500,2000,5000} × {H100,A100-SXM}): Predicts standard Phase 1 (batch=512) correctly identifies the optimal tier in ALL 6 conditions deterministically, while lean Phase 1 fails in ≥2 conditions — establishing that batch=512 is necessary for universal tier-ranking correctness.

Confirmation criteria: h-main confirmed if TPE hits 0.175+ in ≤20 evals; h-control-negative confirmed if final score ≤0.130 (≥20% below 0.1623); h-ablation confirmed if TPE's evals_to_95pct < LHS's in 2/3 seeds; h-robustness confirmed if standard Phase 1 gives consistent correct tiers across all 6 conditions and lean Phase 1 fails in ≥2.
